notes: Simple single-loop AC circuit. Net map (4 nets): n1 = left rail — top lead of V-AC 3 up the x~80 vertical to the corner at (80,182), then right to the left end of Resistor 2 (30ohm). n2 = right end of Resistor 2 to the left bar of the parallel block at x~209, which feeds the left ends of Resistor 0 (50ohm, upper branch) and Capacitor 1 (50uF, lower branch) — verified at 8x that the block is a closed rectangle with the incoming lead landing mid-height on the left bar. n3 = right bar of that block at x~287: right ends of Resistor 0 and Capacitor 1, then right along y~183 to the corner at (357,186) and down into the top of Inductor 5 (2mH). 0 = bottom rail at y~312-315 from x~80 to x~357: bottom of Inductor 5, bottom lead of V-AC 3, and GND 4 whose stem T's down off the rail at x~217 (verified at 8x). Judgment calls: (a) Resistor 0 and Capacitor 1 are in PARALLEL, not series — the block's two vertical bars at x~209 and x~287 tie their like ends together; the drafter's labels '50ohm' and '50uF' sit above and below the block respectively. (b) The long faint horizontal strokes at y~140 and y~365 and the verticals at x~5 and x~510 are notebook page rulings; none touches the circuit. (c) Terminal order: V-AC 3 and Inductor 5 are vertical (0 = top, 1 = bottom); Resistors 0 and 2 and Capacitor 1 are horizontal (0 = left, 1 = right). V-AC 3 carries no polarity marks so its order is arbitrary. (d) All six component bboxes are inside the frame — nothing off-frame, nothing unconnected, and nothing was added, removed or re-classed.
